title: Safety Refusal Homogeneity: Do All Models Refuse the Same Prompts and Allow the Same Harms?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: shared permissive zones represent harms that no deployed model catches. This is the most directly dangerous form of safety homogeneity, with immediate implications for harm prevention.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: AILuminate and MLCommons provide validated prompt sets. Running prompts through APIs and mapping refusal boundaries is straightforward. Binary classification (refused/allowed) simplifies analysis.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: 1000 prompts through 15 models, map refusal boundaries, compute overlap. Clear success criteria and a well-defined output. Achievable in 30 hours with pre-existing prompt sets.

novelty.reasoning: The concept of alignment homogeneity and shared refusal patterns is directly addressed in recent work. 'When Safety Becomes a Vulnerability: Exploiting LLM Alignment Homogeneity' (arXiv:2603.03919, 2026) explicitly identifies shared refusal criteria as 'alignment homogeneity' and shows restricted risk contexts transfer across models. Sorry-Bench (ICLR 2025) and SAGE (EMNLP 2025) provide comprehensive safety evaluation frameworks across models. Refusal-Aware Red Teaming (EMNLP 2025) exposes inconsistency in LLM refusal behaviors. However, the specific deliverable — mapping refusal boundaries with 1000 prompts across 15 models to identify shared permissive zones where no model refuses — has not been published as a systematic empirical study with that specific focus on permissive overlap.
